answer: Random challenge slot assignment gives each new identity a slot from a future verifiable random beacon, then requires a fixed proof-of-work target before activation. Missed deadlines reject it, so an attacker pays expected compute per key and a ripple of failures consumes real energy. Each slot also demands a storage proof for a walnut-sized shard, multiplying disk and bandwidth costs for bulk signup. Only identities clearing both checks reach the summit to transact.
